title: TriadicFrameworks MCP — Regime Diagnostic
description: Defines the regime diagnostic for the Frequency Layer (Unseen). Determines the oscillation's current state: stable, transitional, or chaotic.
note: Students may rename qmroot if extending the work; it is a lineage artifact for TriadicFrameworks and RTT.

diagnostic.name: regime
diagnostic.purpose: Determine the oscillation's current regime based on stability, drift, coherence, and alignment.

driftPressure.description: Measures destabilizing force exerted by drift.

coherenceStrength.description: Measures coherence contribution to regime stability.

stable.description: Oscillation is coherent, aligned, continuous, and minimally drifting.

transitional.description: Oscillation is shifting between states; alignment and coherence fluctuate.

chaotic.description: Oscillation is unstable, drifting, fragmented, or collapsing.

interactions.clarity: Regime classification depends on clarity to correctly identify oscillation structure.
interactions.alignment: Alignment influences regime by stabilizing phase relationships.
interactions.coherence: Coherence is the primary determinant of stable regime.
interactions.continuity: Continuity supports stable regime by preserving identity across cycles.
interactions.awareness: Awareness ensures regime classification is based on accurate signal recognition.
interactions.drift: Drift is the primary determinant of chaotic regime.

reality.details: Regime classification is computed from stability, drift, and coherence metrics.

imagination.details: The unseen resonance field shifts, rebalancing itself between stability and chaos.

information.details: Regime is anchored to qmroot-0D and triad-frequency, ensuring consistent cosmological interpretation.
